items.title: Two teenage girls killed after car loses control and crashes into motorcycle in Teluk Intan
items.summary: IPOH, July 27 — Two teenage girls were killed after the motorcycle they were riding was involved in a crash on Jalan Padang Tembak in Teluk Intan yesterday. Hilir Perak police chief ACP Chua Kok Lian said police received a report on the incident at about 6.35 pm. He said the car driver has been detained to assist in the investigation, adding that investigations are ongoing to determine the exact cause of the crash.

items.title: #NSTviral: Low-flying helicopter at Pulau Kapas beach sparks criticism
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A helicopter flying low over a beach at Pulau Kapas, Terengganu, has drawn criticism after its rotor wash sent sand and loose items flying among beachgoers. Another user, @nohanan, likened the pilot to "a reckless 'mat rempit' who got a helicopter licence." Meanwhile, @rahimi.ramlee called on CAAM to revoke the pilot's licence and require the pilot to undergo flight training again.

items.title: Berlin police shoot dead chief suspect in deadly Pride parade attack
items.summary: BERLIN: German police said Sunday they had shot and killed the chief suspect in what officials described as a deadly Islamist attack near the Berlin Pride parade the previous night, the latest ramming assault to hit the country. The attack late Saturday – the first such incident to target the German capital's LGBTQ community – killed one woman and wounded 29 others. Dobrindt said 29 people were injured, some seriously.

items.title: OGX secures Nokia distributorship for Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: OGX Group Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary, OGX Networks Sdn Bhd, has been appointed as an authorised distributor of Nokia's networking infrastructure products and services in Malaysia, expanding the group's enterprise networking portfolio. OGX Networks has signed a three-year distributorship agreement with Nokia Services and Networks Malaysia Sdn Bhd, with an automatic renewal option thereafter. The appointment allows OGX Networks to market and distribute Nokia's networking solutions to its system integrator (SI) customers across Malaysia.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher versus US dollar ahead of Negeri Sembilan state poll
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR:The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Monday, supported by positive domestic sentiment ahead of the Negeri Sembilan state election, an analyst said. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said market participants would be watching how the state election influences national politics, particularly ahead of polling in Negeri Sembilan. Early voting for the Negeri Sembilan state election will take place on Tuesday (July 28), with polling scheduled for Aug 1.

items.title: Oil slips 5pct after US, Iran pause fighting over weekend
items.summary: Brent crude futures fell US$4.89, or 5.05 per cent, to US$91.89 by 0009 GMT after briefly slipping under the key support level of US$90 earlier in the session. US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$84.64 a barrel, down US$4.67, or 5.23 per cent. Brent had reached US$100 per barrel as the conflict, which reduced oil shipments via the Strait of Hormuz, spilled over to the Red Sea, hindering exports from the world's top exporter, Saudi Arabia, via the Bab el-Mandeb strait to Asia.

items.title: Man dies after collapsing during football match in Seremban
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 27 — A local man died after collapsing during a football match held at a field in a residential area in Bandar Ekar Rantau here yesterday. Seremban district police chief ACP Mohd Yatim Osman said the Seremban district police headquarters received a report on the incident at about 11.35 am. Mohd Yatim said the victim had a history of heart disease and was receiving follow-up treatment at the Heart Centre of Sultan Idris Shah Hospital, Serdang, Selangor.

items.title: Malaysia to strengthen regional anti-graft cooperation through Asean-PAC meeting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 27 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will host the 22nd Asean Parties Against Corruption (Asean-PAC) Secretariat Meeting in Melaka from July 28 to 30 to strengthen regional cooperation in combating corruption. MACC Policy, Planning and Research Division director Datuk Rasidah Abdul Karim said the meeting would be officiated by MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman. Rasidah said the meeting would provide a platform for member agencies to discuss emerging corruption challenges, exchange best practices and innovative approaches, and strengthen cooperation in enforcement, prevention, capacity building and integrity initiatives.

items.title: Malaysian arrested in South Korea over fatal stabbing during brawl
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 27 — South Korean police have arrested a Malaysian man in connection with the fatal stabbing of another Malaysian during a group brawl in Eumseong, North Chungcheong Province, The Korea Herald reported yesterday. The South Korean English-language daily newspaper said that the incident occurred at about 3 am yesterday at a commercial building, where around 10 people from two rival groups had allegedly gathered after agreeing in advance to fight. According to the report, the suspect allegedly stabbed a Malaysian man in his 20s during the confrontation, leaving him critically injured.

items.title: Police detain two more over alleged abuse linked to Penang boy’s death
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 27 — A foreign man and woman have been remanded for seven days to assist investigations into the death of a five-year-old boy in Gelugor here on Thursday. “Police have now detained four individuals to assist investigations, including the boy’s mother, an Indonesian national, and her Bangladeshi boyfriend,” he told Bernama when contacted yesterday. He said the post-mortem found that the boy died from head and body injuries caused by blunt force impact.

items.title: Anwar congratulates Aniq Kasdan on Malaysia’s first Commonwealth Games gold
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 27 —Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated national weightlifter Mohamad Aniq Kasdan on delivering the first 2026 Commonwealth Games gold medal for Malaysia yesterday. Mohamad Aniq won the gold medal in the men’s 60 kilogramme (kg) weightlifting event at Scottish Event Campus (SEC) Armadillo in Glasgow, Scotland today with a combined lift of 273 kg - 121 kg in the snatch and 152 kg in the clean and jerk - setting a new Games record. He beat silver medalist Rishikanta Singh Chanambam of India, who lifted 264 kg and Joshua Amunga Mboya of Kenya, who secured the bronze with a lift of 260 kg.

items.title: Ayob Khan says world-class police force needs independent law enforcement
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 27 — The Royal Malaysian Police (PDRM) must be given the space to enforce the law independently regardless of position or background if the country wants to have a world-class police force. Deputy Inspector-General of Police, Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay said firm action without favoritism is the main key to ensuring that PDRM continues to be respected and trusted by the community. Earlier, Bukit Aman Special Branch director Datuk Seri Ibrahim Darus was appointed as the Acting Deputy Inspector-General of Police starting today.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan voters should judge manifestos by delivery, not promises, says Tengku Zafrul
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, July 27 — Voters should assess the manifestos of parties contesting the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election based on their ability to translate pledges into action, rather than merely the promises made during the election campaign. Senior political advisor to Prime Minister Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz said that while all parties had their own priorities and commitments, the key consideration was whether they had the ability to fulfil the promises made after receiving the people’s mandate. “Over the past two years and eight months, based on the Negeri Sembilan PH government’s track record, many of the commitments outlined have already been implemented.

items.title: Two teenage girls killed in Teluk Intan crash
items.summary: IPOH: Two teenage girls were killed when the motorcycle they were riding was involved in a crash on Jalan Padang Tembak in Teluk Intan yesterday. Hilir Perak police chief Assistant Commissioner Chua Kok Lian said police received a report on the incident about 6.35pm. He said the car driver has been detained to assist investigations.

items.title: Asyraf Wajdi urges Education Ministry to follow Mara's army veteran warden initiative
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry should consider appointing full-time wardens among army veterans to curb bullying in schools, said Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki. He said this follows an increasing number of bullying cases reported in schools nationwide. "Deploying veterans as wardens would provide them with employment opportunities while instilling greater discipline among students," he added.

items.title: NS polls: Small group engagements more meaningful than big rallies, says Mat Sabu
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: Simple yet meaningful campaign approaches centred on small-group engagements rather than large political rallies allow leaders to connect more personally with voters, says Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu. With just days remaining before polling for the Negri Sembilan election, he said he would continue touring the state to meet residents face-to-face. Earlier, he said his visit to Ulu Senaling carried sentimental value as he had lived in Kuala Pilah for two years under a restricted residence order between 1984 and 1986.

items.title: Beyond Property - Why China's Real Economic Challenge Is Household Confidence
items.summary: The Crisis Is Not Housing—It Is Confidence China's greatest economic challenge today is no longer whether it can manufacture more electric vehicles, dominate advanced semiconductors or lead the global race in artificial intelligence. For more than three decades, China's rise rested on rapid urbanisation, infrastructure investment and an expanding property market. Property sales financed local governments through land revenues, while housing became the principal store of household wealth, the dominant form of collateral and the financial foundation of China's expanding middle class.

items.title: Singapore central bank surprises with policy tightening
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore's central bank unexpectedly tightened its monetary policy on Monday. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said it would slightly increase the prevailing rate of appreciation of its exchange rate-based policy band, which is known as the Singapore dollar nominal effective exchange rate (S$NEER). A majority of analysts polled by Reuters had expected the MAS to hold its policy settings steady.

items.title: Succession Planning: Replanting Leadership in Oil Palm
items.summary: Fruit must be harvested at the right moment. Roads must be maintained before rain turns discipline into drama. Plantation leadership was once shaped mainly by field command.

items.title: Gobind: No automatic sharing of private biometric data [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Private biometric data and building access records collected by smart developments will not be automatically integrated into government systems as Malaysia expands its AI Cities network, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said. Addressing privacy concerns, he said the government's push to develop an "AI Nation" was not aimed at creating a mass surveillance system. To ensure such initiatives operate within a common national framework, Gobind said the government had established a cross-ministry AI Cities Task Force under the Malaysia Digital 2030 Action Plan (MD2030).

items.title: Japan June services producer prices rise as Iran war keeps freight costs high
items.summary: TOKYO: Japan's services producer price index rose 3.2 per cent in June from a year earlier, central bank data showed on Monday, a sign of broadening inflationary pressure that will keep alive market expectations for further interest rate hikes. The annual rise in the index, which tracks the price companies charge each other for services, followed a revised 3.4 per cent gain in May. The increase was driven by continued gains in transportation costs, which rose 5.3 per cent in June from a year earlier, as rising fuel prices and supply disruptions from the Middle East conflict kept ocean and air freight charges elevated, the data showed.

items.title: AI changes how Malaysians buy products
items.summary: Industry players said the shopping journey is no longer linear, as consumers move between online and offline channels multiple times before making a purchase. SingleInterface Southeast Asia director Punit Sharma said Malaysia is well positioned to benefit from this shift, supported by its high level of digital adoption and strong small and medium enterprise (SME) ecosystem. Despite the opportunities, Punit said many SMEs struggle to manage multiple digital platforms while operating with limited marketing budgets.

items.title: Corporate demand for AI training doubles, says PEOPLElogy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping Malaysia's workplaces, with demand for AI-related corporate training doubling this year as businesses race to equip employees with new skills. PEOPLElogy Bhd founder and managing director Allen Lee said organisations are increasingly investing in practical AI training as it becomes more deeply embedded in the workplace. AI Is More Than Just Another Tool Despite the growing adoption, Lee said many people still underestimate AI's capabilities.

items.title: Malaysia stands out as global firms diversify supply chains
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is well positioned to benefit from the ongoing diversification of global supply chains, supported by its mature industrial ecosystem, skilled workforce and strategic location, according to Citi's top executive. Citi Asia South head Amol Gupte said companies are redesigning their supply chains to make them more resilient, with production and sourcing spread across multiple markets instead of being concentrated in a single country. Gupte said Malaysia has secured an attractive position in this evolving landscape, particularly in electronics and advanced manufacturing.

items.title: Iran halts strikes as Trump gives space to talks
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran and the United States held their fire Sunday, handing Gulf shipping and the oil industry a respite from missile strikes as Donald Trump's UN envoy said the president was "giving talks some space." Iran said it had halted retaliatory attacks against Washington's allies in the Middle East, and US ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz told "Fox News Sunday" that, while forces remained "locked and loaded", Trump would give negotiations "a little bit of room." "These attacks continued until two nights ago, but over the past two nights the Americans have stopped their attacks," said Iran's army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia.

items.title: Shein flags tariff hits after posting quarterly loss ahead of Hong Kong IPO
items.summary: SINGAPORE/BEIJING: Shein swung to a US$99 million quarterly loss due to slowing sales after the US removed an import duty exemption on small packages and a hefty one-time accounting charge, the online retailer's pre-IPO financial filings showed on Sunday. The filing, which lays the groundwork for investor roadshows and official bookbuilding of its much-awaited Hong Kong IPO, showed that Shein posted a loss in the first quarter of 2026 compared with a net income of US$395 million a year earlier. Shein's US revenue fell 14.3 per cent to US$2.04 billion in the first quarter from US$2.38 billion a year earlier.

items.title: PJ food court traders choose flood risk over relocation
items.summary: The traders said they welcomed the construction of a flood retention pond next to the food court, but were unwilling to move as it was unclear whether it would be temporary or permanent. Medan Selera PJ Lestari Traders Association chairman Farahanim Ahmad, 43, said mayor Datuk Mohamad Zahri Samingon had given traders the option of relocating during construction. But traders here have decided to stay put," she said.

items.title: Malaysia's agarwood industry gathers steam
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's efforts to develop a high-value agarwood industry are gaining steam, with private sector players expanding production and commercial cultivation months after the government identified the commodity as a promising new growth area. In February, plantation and commodities minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said Malaysia has significant untapped potential in the agarwood industry, which he estimated to be worth about US$1 billion globally. Agartech chairman Datuk Hishamuddin Abdul Karim said the company currently produces about 600,000 MyKynam hybrid agarwood seedlings annually from two nurseries spanning 5.26 hectares in Lendu, Melaka.

items.title: Malaysia gains tariff edge over Asean rivals
items.summary: "The United States did not lower Malaysia's tariffs. Malaysia's competitive position has," he said. Besides Malaysia, Indonesia and Cambodia also remain in the 10 per cent tariff tier.

items.title: Explainer: Trump’s new 10pc tariffs on Malaysia, what’s exempted and what comes next
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 27 — US President Donald Trump introduced fresh tariffs against Malaysia and dozens of other trading partners, just five months after the US Supreme Court quashed his earlier unilateral tariffs. The latest levy is applied under the US’ Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 for Malaysia’s alleged failure to eliminate forced labour in its supply chain. Trump’s erratic tariffs are expected to hurt Malaysia’s export-oriented economy as the US is currently Malaysia’s largest export destination and its second-largest trading partner.

items.title: Citrawarna 2026 showcases Malaysia's culture to global audiences
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Citrawarna 2026 drew more than 700 visitors from 12 countries, with international guests experiencing one of Malaysia's biggest cultural showcases under Visit Malaysia 2026. [[nid:1497733]] Present was Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing. Citrawarna features four signature experiences: Colours of Parade, Colours of Flavour, Colours of Culture and Colours of Art.

items.title: Students find alternative paths after missing out on public university places
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Missing out on a public university placement is not the end of the road, as scholarships and a wide range of higher education options are available at other institutions. She later secured a scholarship to pursue a degree in psychology at a private university. Meanwhile, associate creative director Fahrul Fahlevi Fuad, 32, from Shah Alam, said he pursued higher education at a private university after missing out on a public university placement, thanks to his family's support.

items.title: 12 policemen nabbed after Vanuatu citizen claims RM2 million extortion bid [WATCH]
items.summary: Sources said the victim had paid US$140,000 (RM560,000) to the suspects. The victim lodged a report at the Dang Wangi district police headquarters, prompting an investigation. Dang Wangi police chief Assistant Commissioner Sazalee Adam confirmed the arrests.

items.title: Unequal access leaves students behind in varsity race
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The public university admission system is structured and transparent, but unequal access to information, guidance and opportunities can leave some school leavers at a disadvantage. Visiting fellow at the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute Ooi Kok Hin said UPUOnline, the central public university admission portal, has clear criteria, but students' chances of securing places are often shaped long before they submit their applications, including by their pre-university pathways and access to guidance. Ooi said while the Internet has improved access to information, it has not levelled the playing field, especially for rural and low-income students who may not know where to find guidance.

items.title: Varsity admissions: TVET, micro-credentials offer employability pathways
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Students who failed to get places in public universities still have options, including polytechnics, micro-credentials, professional qualifications and the accreditation of prior experiential learning (Apel), experts said. The advice came after 62,102 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) leavers failed to secure places through the Higher Education Ministry's UPUOnline system for the 2026/2027 academic session. The central public university admission portal received 235,852 applications from SPM leavers, of which 235,480 could be processed.

items.title: Manifestos take centre stage as Negri Sembilan campaign enters final stretch
items.summary: Pakatan Harapan outlined 10 commitments through its "Kekal Harapan" manifesto, which it said was a continuation of policies it had implemented while setting a new direction to advance the state towards 2045. Barisan Nasional, meanwhile, wants to restore the state's development momentum through its "Hebatkan Semula Negeri Sembilan: Kestabilan Dibina, Negeri Dijaga, Rakyat Dibela, Kemakmuran Dicipta" manifesto. BN has proposed setting up a unit to monitor manifesto implementation.

items.title: Survey: Malaysian consumers moving away from crisis-mode response amid improved outlook; fewer plan to cut dining out first
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 27 — Malaysians in a survey are now less pessimistic about their household financial situation, when compared against March and April — which was shortly after the US-Iran conflict or crisis began. Consumer research company Rakuten Insight, which has been tracking Malaysian consumer sentiment through an online survey called the Malaysia Cost Pressure Pulse (MCPP), said its latest survey showed Malaysian consumer sentiment recovering sharply in July, when compared to survey results in April. Survey finds shift from ‘panic’ in April to ‘patience’ in July, and normalising spending behaviour In the same tracker, the share of Malaysian respondents whose first response to a sudden rise in expenses would be to cut discretionary spending fell from 53.5 per cent (April) to 44.7 per cent (July).

items.title: Iran threatens response to Ukraine attack on its ship in Caspian Sea
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Sunday warned that his country would respond to a deadly attack by Ukraine on an Iranian ship in the Caspian Sea. It came after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv had carried out long-range strikes in the Caspian Sea against vessels transporting military cargo involving Iran, underscoring the increasingly international dimensions of Russia's war in Ukraine. Iran's foreign ministry said the attack caused the ship "to explode, killing one sailor and injuring several others."

items.title: Fahmi calls on youth to embrace patriotism, Internet skills
items.summary: JEMPOL: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said secondary school students must develop strong patriotic values and digital literacy to face today's challenges. Fahmi said an emphasis on nationhood and history is crucial to help citizens understand their role in developing the country. Fahmi was speaking after a dialogue with 60 Form Six students under the Pentarama X Kelab Malaysiaku programme and the Safe Internet Campaign at the Jempol information office.

items.title: 'Reforms must follow Sara boost'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Higher Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) handouts will provide short-term relief to struggling households, but broader reforms are needed to address rising costs of living. Universiti Teknologi Mara's Faculty of Business and Management senior lecturer Dr Mohamad Idham Md Razak said the spending generated by the aid would also stimulate the economy. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim recently announced that the government would increase Sara soon.

items.title: Polytechnic student killed in four‑motorcycle crash along Changlun‑Kuala Perlis road
items.summary: ARAU, July 26 — A polytechnic student was killed after the motorcycle he was riding was involved in a crash with three other motorcycles along the Changlun-Kuala Perlis road at Kampung Banat here early today. Arau District Police chief Supt Ahmad Mohsin Md Rodi said the 19-year-old victim, who suffered head injuries and a fractured right leg, was pronounced dead while receiving treatment at the Emergency Unit of the Tuanku Fauziah Hospital (HTF) in Kangar at 7.38 am. He said personnel at the enquiry counter of the Arau District Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division (BSPTD) received information about the crash at 2.10 am.

items.title: Deputy IGP Ayob Khan departs with hard‑hitting message: Integrity over corruption, courage above fear
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — In his retirement speech, Deputy Inspector-General of Police (DIGP) Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay today gave a firm reminder to the rest of the police force about the importance of maintaining integrity and not giving in to corruption. Throughout his nearly 35 years in the police force, Ayob Khan said some of his past decisions had caused him to be misunderstood, but said he had learnt as a police officer to not only do the easy things. Ayob Khan said the police force has taught him the meaning of courage, loyalty and sacrifice, and urged his fellow police officers to uphold the police force’s integrity and reputation.

items.title: Police: Farmer spraying pesticides discovers sack with skeletal remains at Kangar farm
items.summary: KANGAR, July 26 — Skeletal remains believed to be human were found in a sack at a farm opposite a factory here today. District police chief ACP Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop said police received information on the discovery at 10.20am after a man spotted the sack while spraying pesticides at his farm. “The remains have been sent to the Forensic Unit of Tuanku Fauziah Hospital (HTF) here for further investigation,” he said in a statement.

items.title: Sepang roars back as Malaysia secures Bahrain F1 Grand Prix, PM Anwar hails triumph
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 26 — Malaysia will host the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at Sepang International Circuit this year, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today, hailing it as proof of the nation’s readiness to stage world class events. Anwar said he had spoken with Bahrain’s Crown Prince and Prime Minister, His Royal Highness Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, as well as Formula 1 President and CEO Stefano Domenicali, and expressed appreciation for Bahrain’s trust in Malaysia. It reflects the enduring friendship, mutual trust and close partnership between Malaysia and the Kingdom of Bahrain, while reaffirming Malaysia’s readiness and capability to host major international events,” he said.

items.title: PM Anwar extends condolences to families of six killed in Bentong crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the families of the six victims who were killed in a road crash along Jalan Karak Lama in Bentong, Pahang, early yesterday. In a post on X today, Anwar said he and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, were deeply saddened by the tragedy. “My condolences to all the victims’ family members.

items.title: Ayob Khan retires as deputy IGP today after 35 years in police force, Ibrahim now acting DIGP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Outgoing Deputy Inspector-General of Police (DIGP) Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay today handed over his duties as he retires from the police force. In a ceremony witnessed by Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail at the Police Training Centre (Pulapol), Ayob handed over his duties as deputy IGP to Bukit Aman’s Special Branch director Datuk Seri Ibrahim Darus. Throughout his 35-year career, Ayob had held various positions before becoming the DIGP, including as head of Bukit Aman’s Special Branch’s counter-terrorism division, Johor police chief, Bukit Aman’s Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director, and Bukit Aman’s Criminal Investigation Department director.

items.title: Typhoon Noul forces Malaysia Airlines to cancel flights to Shenzhen and Hong Kong
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Malaysia Airlines has cancelled several flights between Kuala Lumpur, Shenzhen and Hong Kong as Typhoon Noul brings severe weather to southern China, disrupting air travel across the region. The airline said services scheduled for July 25 and 26 — MH522 (Kuala Lumpur–Shenzhen), MH523 (Shenzhen–Kuala Lumpur), MH078 (Kuala Lumpur–Hong Kong) and MH079 (Hong Kong–Kuala Lumpur) — were called off due to deteriorating conditions linked to the approaching typhoon. Checks on AirAsia’s flight status page showed similar disruptions, with flight AK126 from Kuala Lumpur to Shenzhen cancelled on Sunday.

items.title: Senior police officers among 12 arrested in alleged RM2m extortion of Chinese national
items.summary: Citing unnamed sources, the newspaper said the victim paid US$140,000 (RM572,000) before later lodging a police report at the Dang Wangi district police headquarters. “He later came forward to lodge a report at the Dang Wangi District Police Headquarters (IPD). Dang Wangi district police chief Assistant Commissioner Sazalee Adam confirmed the arrests when contacted by Utusan Malaysia .

items.title: DPM Zahid: No one above the law if implicated in Tabung Haji RCI report
items.summary: TAMPIN, July 26 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has stressed that no one is above the law if their names are implicated in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). Ahmad Zahid, who is also Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said the RCI findings must be made known transparently, and if there are elements of wrongdoing, appropriate action can be taken according to due legal process. Asked whether the release of the report would affect BN’s campaign in the Negeri Sembilan state election, Ahmad Zahid, who is also UMNO president, said he did not think it would have an impact as people in the state are capable of making mature and wise assessments.

items.title: Bukit Aman: Six to be charged over RM7m Petaling Jaya kidnapping tomorrow as two suspects become prosecution witnesses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Six men will be charged tomorrow over the RM7 million ransom kidnapping in Petaling Jaya after police completed their investigation into the case, while two other suspects have been released to become prosecution witnesses. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Comm Datuk M. Kumar said in a statement that the investigation paper into the case, reported on July 17, was referred to the Attorney General’s Chambers on July 24, which subsequently directed that charges be brought against the six suspects. The six are due to appear before the Petaling Jaya Sessions Court at 9.30am tomorrow.

items.title: Sabah Immigration denies viral claim of Filipino detainee deaths at depot
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, July 26 — The Sabah Immigration Department has denied a viral claim alleging that many Filipino detainees had died due to overcrowding at the state’s immigration detention depots. State Immigration director Datuk SH Sitti Saleha Habib Yussof said that the allegation was false, baseless and misleading. “All Filipino detainees housed at the Immigration detention depots in Sabah are in good condition while awaiting repatriation to their home country,” she said in a statement today.

items.title: Ahead of 60th anniversary, King’s royal diplomacy elevates Russia-Malaysia ties, says ambassador
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — The royal diplomacy of Malaysia’s King, Sultan Ibrahim, has brought the people of Russia and Malaysia closer despite the geographical distance between the two countries, while elevating bilateral ties to a new sphere, Russian Ambassador to Malaysia Naiyl Latypov said. Praising His Majesty's royal approach, Latypov said the King's diplomacy has elevated Russia-Malaysia bilateral ties as the two countries prepare to mark the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations next year. "Russia highly appreciates His Majesty’s royal diplomacy.

items.title: Former PM Muhyiddin says it should be PAS exiting Perikatan, not Bersatu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Bersatu president Muhyiddin Yassin has pushed back against calls for his party to leave Perikatan Nasional (PN), arguing that PAS — not Bersatu — should be the one to step away from the coalition after choosing to end political cooperation between the two parties. FMT reported Muhyiddin saying said Bersatu, as a co‑founder of PN, could not be forced out of the coalition and retained every right to remain. PAS ended its cooperation with Bersatu early last month, though both remain PN components.

items.title: Mohamad Hasan says non-Malays have ‘no reason to be unduly worried’ by BN-Perikatan pact in Negeri Sembilan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Barisan Nasional (BN) has assured non-Malay voters they will not be sidelined if the coalition secures victory in the upcoming Negeri Sembilan state election, despite its cooperation with Perikatan Nasional (PN). According to The Star , BN deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said claims by rivals that minorities would be marginalised were unfounded, stressing that BN remained the dominant force in the partnership. He added that seven of BN’s seats had been allocated to MCA and two to MIC, while PN was also fielding non-Muslim candidates.

items.title: Malaysian students breathe easier as Australia spares Asean neighbours from visa fee surge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Australia has imposed a sharp 25 per cent rise in international student visa fees but carved out an exemption for applicants from Asean nations, including Malaysia, as part of efforts to deepen regional ties. “A reduced visa fee rate for students from Asean nations reflects the importance Australia places on welcoming high quality students from South-east Asia,” Assistant Minister for International Education Julian Hill told Singapore’s The Straits Times (ST). Australia already applies lower fees for Pacific nations, including Timor Leste, which joined Asean in October 2025, as part of its diplomatic outreach.

items.title: Nadma: Disaster victims can claim cash aid up to four times a year
items.summary: JERTIH, July 26 — Malaysians affected by disasters are eligible to receive the Bantuan Wang Ihsan (BWI) up to four times a year, subject to the claim conditions set by the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma). Nadma Community and Social Development Section director Jefny Muhammad said the assistance is provided to ease the burden of victims affected by disasters such as floods, landslides, fires, tidal waves and other calamities. Jefny said 108,000 heads of household nationwide received BWI amounting to RM108 million during the 2025/2026 Northeast Monsoon season.

items.title: Housewife loses RM119,599 to Facebook investment scam
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, July 26 —A housewife lost RM119,599.24 after falling victim to an investment scam on July 19. Kota Tinggi police chief Supt Yusof Othman said the 58-year-old woman came across an advertisement for an investment scheme, identified as XM Royal, on Facebook. Yusof said the victim realised she had been scammed after failing to receive the promised investment returns despite making several payments.

items.title: Temporary shelters house families in flood-stricken Melaka Tengah and Jasin
items.summary: MELAKA, July 26 —The number of flood victims in Melaka rose to 124 people from 37 families as of 8 am today, with three temporary relief centres still operating in Melaka Tengah and Jasin. In Melaka Tengah, 55 victims from 17 families are taking shelter at the Pantai Kundor Japerun Hall. while 44 victims from 12 families are placed at SK Serkam Darat and 25 victims from eight families at SK Bukit Tembakau in Jasin.

items.title: Scammer poses as government official, contractor loses over RM50,000
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, July 26 — A 52-year-old electrical wiring contractor lost RM50,400 after falling victim to a fake government tender offer scam. Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the victim received an email on July 14 containing a quotation request for the installation of solar LED street lights purportedly under a special local authority allocation. “The victim, who believed the offer was genuine, made two payments totalling RM50,400 to two separate bank accounts on July 23 using business funds.

items.title: PM Anwar attends Citrawarna 2026 launch and cultural parade
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim attended the opening ceremony and parade of Citrawarna 2026 at Dataran Merdeka yesterday, a flagship Tourism Malaysia event held as part of the Visit Malaysia 2026 (VM2026) campaign. He was joined by Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing, Deputy Minister Chiew Choon Man, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Tourism Malaysia director-general Mohd Amirul Rizal Abdul Rahim. Supported by Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL), Warisan Kuala Lumpur, the National Department for Culture and Arts (JKKN), Istana Budaya and the National Textile Museum, Citrawarna 2026 aims to promote Malaysia’s arts, culture and heritage tourism to domestic and international visitors.
